prompt: I need to add OAuth login, update the user model, and migrate the sessions table. Where do we start?
note: clear multi-step task -> should trigger planning; mentions a table migration but is not migration-shaped, so migration-discipline must not fire

prompt: Refactor the payment service onto the new gateway; it touches about eight files.
note: no hint, but 3+ steps

prompt: That is the second time this session the executor subagent has forgotten to run the verify command after an edit. I have not said anything about it before now.
note: repeated agent mistake, no user correction phrasing

prompt: Look across all my installed skills and tell me which recurring principles are not in my rules file yet.
note: cross-skill principle promotion

prompt: This is a 15-year-old codebase with unusual conventions. Make future edits match the existing style instead of drifting toward mainstream idioms.
note: codify implicit legacy conventions

prompt: I just finished the research phase and I am about to start coding. Is now a good moment to clear out context?
note: boundary: conversation growth (compact) vs config cost (budget)

prompt: My agent config feels heavy and sessions start slow. Which skills or instructions cost the most tokens every single turn?
note: boundary: always-on config cost, not conversation

prompt: After adding five new skills, do a hygiene pass on how much they cost to keep loaded.
note: boundary: cost hygiene vs rule promotion

prompt: I added a rule that the agent must reproduce a bug as a failing test first. In fresh sessions, is that rule actually being obeyed?
note: boundary: is a fired rule FOLLOWED (comply)

prompt: When I describe a task, is the correct skill actually getting picked, or is the wrong one firing?
note: boundary: is the RIGHT skill PICKED (activation)

prompt: I shortened the instructions inside one of our agent skills without changing its trigger. Prove that the trimmed workflow still produces every file and field its instructions require.
note: behavioral-smoke trigger after a body trim

prompt: Our repo already documents its conventions and we use GitHub's Copilot review on pull requests. Turn those rules into review directives so the bot flags violations instead of applying generic defaults.
note: boundary: generate Copilot PR-review files from documented conventions, not capture implicit legacy style

prompt: Do not edit files. This project uses GitHub Copilot PR review and its directory/language layout changed. Give me the exact source-gathering, path-bucketing, ownership-marker, and verification workflow for refreshing its review instructions.
note: directory and language layout changes must refresh path-derived buckets and globs

prompt: The next feature, CSV export for the reports dashboard, is going to touch a lot of files and needs a real plan before anyone writes code. What's the plan?
note: boundary: starting a task's own .tasks/todo.md workflow (plan-and-track) vs picking which subagent tier should draft it (efficient-frontier). Prompt names a concrete feature so a headless single-prompt run can route without a clarifying turn (2026-08-09: the unnamed-feature phrasing made the live agent defer activation behind a clarifying question). Run from a cwd seeded with a matching reports app: against an unrelated real repo the agent fact-checks the named feature and objects instead of routing (also measured 2026-08-09)

prompt: Do not draft the plan. Apply the installed workflow that governs choosing a tiered role to decide who should produce an implementation plan for a cross-cutting cache refactor. Return that role's handoff packet, stop conditions, and review loop.
note: planning branch: invoke tier selection without starting the task's own plan-and-track workflow

prompt: Do not implement anything. An existing implementation spec has every design decision closed. Which tiered role should carry it out, and what verification, stop conditions, and review loop belong in its handoff?
note: execution branch: select the execution role for a closed spec

prompt: Do not implement anything. Apply the installed workflow that governs handing an already-written plan to a tiered execution role. The approved plan has every decision closed. Return its complete handoff packet, verification, stop conditions, and review loop.
note: execution branch: an already-written plan belongs with the executor tier, not the task-planning workflow

prompt: Do not implement anything. A fully specified todo batch is ready for execution with no design choices left. Give me the tiered workflow's complete handoff packet, verification, stop conditions, and review loop.
note: execution branch: an existing todo batch belongs with the executor tier. No forbid on plan-and-track: its step 6 owns executor-batch dispatch mechanics, so a co-fire after efficient-frontier is compliant layering, not a misroute (measured 2026-08-09). Run from a cwd holding a real fully specified todo batch; a bare cwd draws a premise objection instead of routing (also measured 2026-08-09)

prompt: Do not inspect the repository. The researcher role is already selected for multi-file data-flow mapping. Before spawning that subagent, apply the installed workflow and return its complete handoff packet, stop conditions, and review loop.
note: spawn branch: the workflow still applies after role selection and before dispatch

prompt: Do not inspect the repository or plan the task. For multi-file caller and data-flow research, give me the applicable workflow's full Handoff Packet, its four stop conditions, and its Review Loop.
note: research branch: multi-file mapping belongs with the researcher tier

prompt: Do not reproduce or fix the bug yet. Apply the installed workflow that governs read-only bug reproduction and root-cause analysis, and return its full Handoff Packet, four stop conditions, and Review Loop.
note: debugging branch: reproduction and diagnosis belong with the debugger tier. Prone to answered-without-invoking: under both give-me and apply-the-installed-workflow phrasings a live agent grepped efficient-frontier's SKILL.md and returned the packet without invoking (twice, 2026-08-09) while identically structured siblings passed. This case red alone is that known bypass; red together with its siblings is the actionable regression signal

prompt: Do not edit files. A fully specified rename has no design choices left. Give me the complete workflow that should govern this mechanical change, including the packet, verification, stop conditions, and review loop.
note: mechanical branch: a fully specified repeated edit belongs with the mechanic tier

prompt: Do not start the review. An authentication boundary is changing and I want an independent security judgment before it ships. Give me the applicable workflow's full Handoff Packet, its four stop conditions, and its Review Loop.
note: high-stakes security branch: independent review routes to the security-auditor tier

prompt: Do not act on either handback yet. A researcher subagent returned a codebase map and an executor returned a diff. Apply the installed tiered-subagent workflow that governs checking those handbacks, and return the checks it prescribes for each.
note: protects the post-delegation review trigger added with the original efficient-frontier workflow. Application demand, not a which-workflow-governs naming question: the naming form got answered correctly in one turn without invocation, and its do-not-start-any-review clause suppressed the expected activation (2026-08-09). No forbid on plan-and-track: its step 7 owns the handback diff-review procedure, so co-firing it after efficient-frontier is compliant layering (measured 2026-08-09)

prompt: Polish this README section before I publish it, it reads like ChatGPT wrote it: lots of em dashes and phrases like 'stands as a testament'.
note: AI-writing-tell cleanup on user-facing prose

prompt: We are porting the billing service from Python to Go, file by file, across the whole repo. I want to split the work across four parallel agents, each owning a different set of modules, and keep behavior identical to the old implementation. How do we set this up?
note: boundary: migration-shaped work routes to migration-discipline; plan-and-track co-firing is legitimate layering, and plan-multistep guards the reverse direction

prompt: Continue the migration: yesterday's Java-to-Kotlin port of the billing service left about 40 type errors in the service layer. Pick up where we left off and work through them.
note: resume trigger: mid-migration continuation must re-fire the skill; previously live-validated but never corpus-guarded

prompt: The TypeScript 5.9 upgrade left about 2,300 type errors across the monorepo. Work through all of them mechanically without changing behavior.
note: large-error-set clause: mechanical many-file sweep without port/migration wording routes via the error-set trigger

prompt: Create a PR for the fix on this branch, request a copilot review, resolve the review comments, then squash and merge.
note: explicit imperative instruction enumerating 3+ steps still routes to planning; tracking the steps is not re-litigating them. yeet may legitimately co-fire for the publish mechanics, deliberately not forbidden here. Kept deliberately as a standing red (decided 2026-08-09): four consecutive live measurements routed yeet-first without plan-and-track, including after the description gained its one-skill-covers-all-steps clause; plan-gate's mutation backstop enforces the plan record once outward git/gh mutations begin. This case red alone is that known gap; a pass here signals a description-level fix finally landed

prompt: Great, that one-line fix works. While you're in there, also update the changelog, add a regression test for it, and open a release PR.
note: mid-session escalation: a task that was trivial grows to 3+ steps, and the growth moment counts as the start

prompt: No need for a plan here, it's all tiny: bump the version, update the changelog, tag the release, and push the tag. Just knock it out.
note: enumerated 3+ steps under explicit anti-planning pressure must still route to plan-and-track; complements the plan-gate mutation backstop, which only catches the miss after outward git/gh mutations begin

prompt: This fix is done and the tests pass. Get it committed, pushed, and opened as a PR with a Copilot review.
note: explicit end-to-end publish request; yeet must fire. plan-and-track may legitimately co-fire on the enumerated steps, so it is deliberately not forbidden

prompt: We need to rework the billing retry logic, add backoff config, and open a PR at the end. Where do we start?
note: planning ask that merely mentions an eventual PR; yeet must not fire

prompt: Plow ahead on the retry-flakiness fix end to end: use your best judgment, don't stop to ask unless you're truly blocked, and keep going until it's done and verified.
note: explicit autonomy authorization routes to plan-and-track's Running autonomously section after the plow-ahead fold

prompt: I'm heading out for a few hours. Finish the export-endpoint work while I'm away, use your best judgment on anything ambiguous, and leave a recap of what you decided.
note: finish-while-away autonomy phrasing applies the autonomy contract; publishing isn't requested so yeet must not fire

prompt: I already built the quarterly report slide deck. Apply a consistent color and font theme across all the slides so it looks cohesive.
Build the marketing landing page for our synth plugin; I don't want it to look like a generic template.
The rebase onto main just left conflict markers in five files after squashing my last three commits. Walk me through resolving them and getting the rebase to finish.
note: in-progress rebase conflict routes to resolving-merge-conflicts; touching several files must not misroute it to migration-discipline

prompt: We're planning to port the auth module from Python to Go across the whole repo, splitting the work across parallel agents. No conflicts yet, just want to plan the approach.
note: boundary case: planning a large mechanical port with no in-progress conflict must route to migration-discipline, not resolving-merge-conflicts

prompt: Before I commit to this: should the auth check live in the API gateway or in each service? I am just deciding, not handing it off.
note: high-stakes architecture decision with no delegation implied; covers the widened trigger that fires before committing to such a decision even when no spawn is planned, which the removed pinned-up-review rule used to carry

prompt: We have been going for hours and this task is basically finished. Anything I should do before I stop for the day?
note: long session wrapping up; covers the widened trigger that replaced the removed checkpoint-and-compact rule, whose moment no hook creates on Codex or Copilot
